metrics_cross_help: Among the posts that received a reply in the week, the share whose replies that week came from members of two or more language areas. Weeks start on Monday (UTC); the last row is the current week so far. Each reply is counted under the area its author had when writing it.

metrics_reports_auto: Closed automatically (re-translated, original edited, or deleted)
metrics_reports_median: Median time for a person to resolve
metrics_ai_title: Declared AI assistance (frontmatter and API), by language area
metrics_ai_help: Posts and replies, by the author's language area at the time of writing. Only posts that have an ai_assistance value are counted in the value columns (set through frontmatter or the API; posts written on the website have none). The last column counts posts without a value.
metrics_note: Every rate shows its numerator, its denominator and the number of people behind it. A week or a group with a zero denominator is shown as "Not observed". Members whose stances and Insightful reactions are excluded from counts are not counted, and neither are hidden or deleted posts. When a member withdraws an Insightful reaction or deletes their stance record, the numbers of past weeks go down too.
metrics_insight_help: Of the Insightful reactions given that week on posts whose author's language area is known, the share given by a member in a different language area from the author (both as they were at the time). Two members who are both in "Other" do not count as across languages. Numerator: across languages. Denominator: all such Insightful reactions. People: the members who gave them.
metrics_update_help: Of the stance changes of the week that were prompted by a post (through "Reconsider my stance"), the share where the post was written by someone in another language area than the member's. A first stance and a withdrawal do not count as changes. Numerator: prompted by a post from another area. Denominator: changes that have a prompting post. People: the members in the denominator.
metrics_active_help: Members who, that week, wrote a post or a reply, pressed Insightful, or recorded a stance. Each member is counted once a week.
metrics_retention_help: The members who signed up in the week (the cohort), and how many of them were active in the week that starts 4 weeks after the cohort's week (days 28 to 34). Not observed until that week has ended. Numerator: active then. Denominator and people: the cohort.
metrics_first_title: First stance and first post within 14 days (by sign-up week)
metrics_first_help: The share of each cohort who reached a first stance, and a first post or reply, within 14 days of signing up. The two are counted separately. Not observed until every member of the cohort has had 14 days.
metrics_small_numbers: For operators only. The numbers below are by language area and are summed across questions and posts: this screen never shows the stances of a single question by area. In an area with few members, a number can reflect one person's habits, so every cell shows how many people are behind it. Take care when copying these numbers elsewhere.
metrics_dir_title: Direction of reactions across language areas
metrics_dir_help: Which areas react to the posts of which areas, in total across posts since {from}. Rows: the author's language area when the post was written. Columns: the language area of the member who pressed Insightful or replied. Each cell: the reactions of that pair / all the reactions to the posts of the row's area (people). The diagonal is the same area. A high number off the diagonal in one direction and not in the other shows which way the reactions go.
metrics_distance_title: Distance between the stances of language areas
metrics_distance_help: For each pair of language areas, at the end of each week: the mean, over the questions on which both areas have a stance, of the distance between their stance distributions (0: the same, 1: opposite). It is taken across questions; no number for a single question is shown. The mean also falls when members join or leave, so read it with the number of questions and of people. It is a cue to look closer, not proof that opinions converge. Cell: mean (sum of the distances / questions; people).
metrics_first_stances_help: The first stance each member took on a question, before later reasons and numbers could move them (a new choice after a withdrawal is not a first stance), by the member's language area at the time. Summed across questions over the last 8 weeks, never per question. Cell: first stances that chose this option (column) / all first stances of the area (people).
metrics_langs_help: Questions asked in each original language, per week and over the last 8 weeks (alternative framings included; hidden and deleted ones not). Cell: questions in the language / all questions of the week (people who asked).

observation_export_help: Entry metadata (including whether each entry is a question), translation engines, divergences and the diversity metrics, and for each readable question the totals and the number of languages that members see, for operator use only. It has no email addresses, user IDs, usernames, titles or bodies, no one's stance and no history of stance changes, and authors appear only as keys that change with every export, but it is pseudonymous, not anonymous: entry IDs and timestamps are the forum's own, so anyone who can read the forum can trace rows back to authors. observation_div_help: Per language pair (original language to translation language): how many translations were compared out of all that could be compared (posts, primary engine), the divergence records, and their severity. The judge also looks at tone: when one translation turns a hedged statement (maybe, I think, peut-être) into an assertion, or the reverse, it is recorded as a tone divergence and counted in the "Tone" column. A comparison runs only for the sampled translations (DIVERGENCE_SAMPLE_RATE); the list of divergences is for native speakers to check. The last two columns count the cases where the secondary engine was from the same vendor as the primary, which is a less independent comparison.
observation_div_tone_guide: When you check a divergence, look not only for a difference in meaning but also for a change of tone: a hedged phrasing (such as "maybe" or "I think") that the translation turns into an assertion, or the other way round.
observation_div_off: Divergence detection is off. It runs only when TRANSLATION_SECONDARY and DIVERGENCE_JUDGE are both set, and then only for the share of translations set by DIVERGENCE_SAMPLE_RATE (see docs/deploy.md). Any figures below come from earlier measurements.
observation_div_rate_zero: The sample rate is 0, so no translation is compared. Set DIVERGENCE_SAMPLE_RATE to a number from 0 to 1 (see docs/deploy.md). Any figures below come from earlier measurements.

quality_signals_help: Since {since}. Count each post/reply field and target language once per source revision, excluding flagged copies and hidden output. Title refinement and redoing flagged output do not add to the count; saved report retries count once per field. Chat counts committed translations. Reports per generated translation may exceed 100%. Generation counts exclude older translations; deleted reports leave report totals. Only a changed saved correction or automatic retry counts as corrected, not closing or hiding.
quality_drafts_help: Aggregate of readable published posts from API and MCP drafts recorded since this feature began. Compare the last tool-supplied title/body with the published text. The changed span runs from the first to the last changed character in each field; its share is an upper bound on editing, not an exact edit distance. No member breakdown.

stats_updated: Collected at {at}. Updated about once an hour.
stats_privacy: Counts of participants’ activity are withheld when there are 1–4 items or people. Rates are shown only when the denominator is at least 5 and the numerator is 0 or at least 5. Evaluation results contain no member data, so this rule does not apply to them.
stats_eval_help: The latest completed run using real engines shows the fraction of evaluated checks that preserved meaning, and severe errors, by language pair and category. These results do not measure the accuracy of members’ posts.

stats_translation_help: Weekly counts of post translations still available to readers and chat translations ready to display, grouped by first record creation. Titles and bodies count separately. Deleted or hidden posts and messages, and translations in places that cannot be read (such as closed villages), are excluded. Regeneration calls are also excluded.
stats_pairs_help: Distinct source → target language pairs with readable post translations created or updated in the four weeks from {from} to collection time. Deleted or hidden posts, posts in places that cannot be read (such as closed villages), and chat translations are excluded. Only the count is shown.
stats_report_help: Counts are post reports received each week. The correction rate uses post and chat reports from that week with a known source language since measurement began; its numerator counts actual corrections by collection time, excluding dismissals and closures without corrections.
stats_signals_since: Correction measurement starts at the later of each week’s start and {since}.
stats_reply_help: Of topics receiving replies each week from members with known language areas, the fraction with repliers from at least two areas. People counts members replying to those topics. Deleted and hidden posts are excluded.
stats_insightful_help: Of Insightful reactions given each week to posts with a known author language area, the fraction from a different area. People counts reacting members. Deleted and hidden posts and members excluded from reaction counts are omitted.
stats_active_help: Members with a post, reply, Insightful reaction or stance event each week, counted once per member. Reading alone and deleted or hidden posts do not count. Insightful and stance events omit members excluded from reaction counts.
stats_retention_help: Of members joining in each cohort week, the fraction active in the week starting four weeks later. Not measured until that later week has ended. Members excluded from reaction counts are omitted.

push_privacy_heading: How notification delivery uses your data
push_privacy: Your browser chooses a delivery service: Apple, Google, Mozilla or Microsoft. The service receives a delivery identifier, encrypted notification, sender, time, frequency and size. tomola stores the delivery address and keys, an estimated browser and OS name, registration date and delivery status.
